syllabus.overview: The official JEE (Advanced) syllabus spans Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics (for Paper 1 & Paper 2) and the Architecture Aptitude Test (AAT) for B.Arch. aspirants at IIT Roorkee, IIT Kharagpur, and IIT (BHU) Varanasi.

primary_pdfs.title: JEE (Advanced) 2026 Information Brochure — Complete Official Syllabus (Pages 61–85)

subjects.name: Physics (Paper 1 & Paper 2)
units: General: Units & dimensions, dimensional analysis, least count, significant figures, experimental error analysis (Vernier, screw gauge, simple pendulum, Young's modulus, surface tension, calorimeter, focal length, resonance column, Ohm's law, meter bridge/post office box)

Mechanics: 1D/2D kinematics, Newton's laws, friction, work-energy-power, centre of mass & collisions, rigid body rotation, SHM, gravitation, fluid mechanics & Bernoulli's theorem, mechanical waves & Doppler effect

Thermal Physics: Thermal expansion, calorimetry, 1D heat conduction, convection/radiation, Newton's law of cooling, ideal gas laws, 1st & 2nd laws of thermodynamics, Carnot engine, blackbody radiation
Electricity and Magnetism: Coulomb's law, Gauss's law, capacitance, Ohm's law & Kirchhoff's laws, Biot-Savart & Ampere's laws, moving coil galvanometer, Faraday's & Lenz's laws, RC/LR/LC/LCR circuits
Electromagnetic Waves: Characteristics and full electromagnetic spectrum (radio to gamma rays)
Optics: Reflection/refraction at plane & spherical surfaces, TIR, prisms, thin lenses, Huygens' principle, Young's double-slit interference, single-slit diffraction, polarization & Brewster's law
Modern Physics: Atomic nucleus, alpha/beta/gamma decay, binding energy, fission & fusion, photoelectric effect, Bohr's model, X-rays & Moseley's law, de Broglie wavelength

subjects.name: Chemistry (Paper 1 & Paper 2)
units: General & Physical Chemistry: Concept of atoms/molecules, gaseous & liquid states, atomic structure & chemical bonding, energetics/thermodynamics, chemical & ionic equilibrium, electrochemistry, chemical kinetics, solid state, solutions, surface chemistry
Inorganic Chemistry: Isolation/preparation & properties of non-metals, transition elements (3d series), ores & minerals, extractive metallurgy, principles of qualitative analysis (Groups I–V)
Organic Chemistry — Concepts & Hydrocarbons: Hybridisation, isomerism, inductive/resonance/hyperconjugation effects, alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, benzene, phenols
Organic Chemistry — Functional Groups: Alkyl halides, alcohols, ethers, aldehydes & ketones, carboxylic acids, amines, haloarenes
Biomolecules, Polymers & Everyday Chemistry: Carbohydrates, amino acids/peptides, nucleic acids (DNA/RNA), polymers, therapeutic drug classes, soaps & detergents
Practical Organic Chemistry: Detection of N, S, halogens and alcoholic, phenolic, carbonyl, carboxyl, amino, and nitro functional groups

subjects.name: Mathematics (Paper 1 & Paper 2)
units: Sets, Relations and Functions: Set algebra, De-Morgan's laws, equivalence relations, invertible/even/odd/one-one/onto functions, composition
Algebra: Complex numbers, quadratic equations, AP/GP, logarithms, permutations & combinations, binomial theorem
Matrices: Matrix operations, transpose, elementary transformations, determinants (up to order 3), adjoint, inverse, simultaneous linear equations
Probability and Statistics: Sample space, conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, mean/median/mode, variance & standard deviation, random variables
Trigonometry: Trigonometric functions, periodicity, multiple/sub-multiple angles, trigonometric equations, inverse trigonometric functions
Analytical Geometry (2D & 3D): Straight lines, circles, parabola, ellipse, hyperbola, locus problems; 3D lines, skew lines, planes, shortest distance
Differential Calculus: Limits, continuity, L'Hospital rule, derivatives, chain rule, tangents/normals, maxima/minima, Rolle's & Lagrange's MVT
Integral Calculus: Indefinite & definite integrals, fundamental theorem, integration by parts/substitution/partial fractions, area under curves, 1st-order ODEs
Vectors: Vector addition, scalar multiplication, dot & cross products, scalar & vector triple products

subjects.name: Architecture Aptitude Test (AAT)
subjects.paper: Optional post-JEE (Advanced) test for B.Arch. at IITs
units: 1. Freehand Drawing: Proportion, surface texture, relative location, and day-to-day objects from memory
2. Geometrical Drawing: Lines, angles, polygons, circles, plan (top view) & elevation (front/side views) of solids
3. Three-Dimensional Perception: Building elements, colour, volume, orientation, structuring objects in memory
4. Imagination and Aesthetic Sensitivity: Composition exercises, context mapping, colour grouping
5. Architectural Awareness: Famous national and international architectural creations, places, and architects/designers

exam_pattern.overview: JEE (Advanced) consists of two compulsory Computer Based Test (CBT) papers — Paper 1 and Paper 2 — held on the same day. Exact section-wise question counts and partial-marking rubrics are disclosed in the on-screen CBT instructions on examination day; both papers evaluate Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics.

papers.duration: 3 Hours (09:00 – 12:00 IST) | PwD Compensatory Time: +1 Hour (up to 13:00 IST)
papers.question_types: Single-choice MCQs, Multiple-correct MCQs (with partial marking), Numerical Value / Non-negative integer questions, Matching List / Matrix Match

papers.duration: 3 Hours (14:30 – 17:30 IST) | PwD Compensatory Time: +1 Hour (up to 18:30 IST)
papers.question_types: Single-choice MCQs, Multiple-correct MCQs (with partial marking), Numerical Value / Non-negative integer questions, Matching List / Matrix Match

papers.mode: Pen & Paper Test (Only for JEE Advanced qualified candidates seeking B.Arch.)
papers.subjects: Freehand & Geometrical Drawing, 3D Perception, Aesthetic Sensitivity, Architectural Awareness
papers.question_types: Qualifying test (cut-off marks decided by JIC; admission based on JEE Advanced CRL rank)

marking_scheme.marks: Both Paper 1 and Paper 2 are mandatory; absence in either paper disqualifies the candidate
Full, partial, zero, and negative marks vary by section (e.g., +3/-1 or +4/-2 with partial +1/+2) as printed in each paper's instructions
Bilingual — English and Hindi (candidates can toggle between English and Hindi on screen during the CBT)

mediums: Hindi (Bilingual toggle available on CBT screen)
tie_breaking: 1. Higher positive marks obtained in JEE (Advanced) across both papers combined
4. If tie still persists, candidates are awarded the same rank

eligibility.overview: Indian Nationals and OCI/PIO (I) candidates must simultaneously satisfy all five official criteria (A1–A5) published on jeeadv.ac.in/eligibility.html (2026 rules shown as reference for 2027).

criteria_list.title: Performance in JEE (Main) B.E./B.Tech. Paper
criteria_list.detail: Must be among the top 2,50,000 successful candidates (across all categories) in Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech.) of JEE (Main): 40.5% OPEN (incl. 5% PwD), 10% GEN-EWS, 27% OBC-NCL, 15% SC, 7.5% ST (with 5% horizontal PwD within each category).

criteria_list.title: Age Limit
criteria_list.detail: For 2026: Born on or after October 1, 2001 (5 years relaxation for SC, ST, and PwD candidates: born on or after October 1, 1996).

criteria_list.title: Number of Attempts
criteria_list.detail: Maximum of TWO attempts in TWO consecutive years.

criteria_list.title: Appearance in Class XII (or Equivalent) Examination
criteria_list.detail: Candidate should have appeared for the Class XII (or equivalent) examination for the first time in either the immediately preceding year or the current exam year with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics as compulsory subjects.

criteria_list.title: Earlier Admission at IITs
criteria_list.detail: Candidate should NOT have been admitted to an IIT earlier (irrespective of whether they continued or accepted a seat via JoSAA), except candidates admitted to a preparatory course for the first time in the preceding year.

eligibility.admission_performance_rule: For IIT admission via JoSAA, candidates must also secure at least 75% aggregate marks in Class XII (65% for SC, ST, and PwD) OR be within the category-wise Top 20 Percentile of successful candidates in their respective Class XII Board examination.
eligibility.foreign_and_oci: Foreign National candidates and OCI/PIO (F) candidates register directly on jeeadv.ac.in (exempt from JEE Main Criterion A1) under supernumerary seats up to 10% of total seats per course. OCI/PIO (I) candidates compete under OPEN / OPEN-PwD.

rules: JEE (Advanced) results include Common Rank List (CRL) and category-wise rank lists (GEN-EWS, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD) subject to minimum subject and aggregate percentages.
Qualified candidates must register and fill choices on the JoSAA portal (https://josaa.nic.in/) to participate in seat allocation across all 23 IITs and IISc Bengaluru B.Tech. programmes.
B.Arch. aspirants at IIT Roorkee, IIT Kharagpur, and IIT (BHU) Varanasi must additionally qualify the Architecture Aptitude Test (AAT).
